title: Moonlit Sirocco

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.body: Moonlit Sirocco is tracked against intrusions into Gulf energy operators. This profile consolidates what CPX holds on the actor's objectives, tradecraft, infrastructure and targeting, and states where the picture is incomplete.

sections.heading: Threat Actor Overview
sections.body: Tracked by CPX as Moonlit Sirocco. Aliases carried by vendors differ and are recorded with the vendor that assigned each; no two vendor names are merged automatically. Attribution is assessed at moderate confidence on overlapping infrastructure and tooling, not on a state claim.

sections.heading: Objectives
sections.body: Assessed as collection against operational technology programmes in the regional energy sector. Motivation beyond collection is not evidenced in what CPX holds and is not asserted here.

sections.heading: Modus Operandi
sections.body: Initial access through internet-facing application exploitation and targeted phishing. Execution through scripting interpreters, then credential access and lateral movement toward engineering workstations. Activity has been observed in short, dense windows rather than continuous presence.

sections.heading: Capabilities
sections.body: Commodity loaders paired with a bespoke backdoor observed in the reported activity window. Living-off-the-land execution is preferred over dropped tooling once access is held.

sections.heading: Infrastructure
sections.body: Staging over rented virtual hosts with short lifetimes, and command-and-control over domains registered days before use. Indicators are held raw and render defanged.

sections.heading: Targeted Industries and Victims
sections.body: Energy and utilities across the Gulf region, with observed victims in the UAE. Sectors named without an observed victim are a targeting signal drawn from actor tooling and lures, and are labelled as such rather than reported as compromise.

sections.heading: Diamond Model Analysis
sections.body: The four vertices and the relationships between them, from the evidence held at the time of writing.

sections.heading: MITRE ATT&CK Mapping
sections.body: Techniques observed in the reported activity window, resolved against the held ATT&CK table.

sections.heading: Key Findings and Assessment
sections.body: The actor's infrastructure turnover is faster than its tooling turnover, so detection built on tooling has held longer than detection built on indicators. Assessed at moderate confidence.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.body: Prioritise patching of internet-facing applications in the estate. Hunt for scripting-interpreter execution on engineering workstations. Treat the indicator set as short-lived and prefer behavioural detection.
